title: A little Hindi. A lot to say.
pronunciationTip: Capitals suggest gentle emphasis. aa, ee and oo are long vowels; don’t give Hindi a strong English stress.
pronunciationGuide: Hindi in Roman letters. Capital vowels are gentle pronunciation cues, not fixed Greek-style stress marks. aa, ee and oo mark long vowels. In main, hoon and naheen, the final n signals a nasal vowel. kh, th and bh include a puff of breath; th is not the English sound in ‘think’. Choose masculine or feminine phrasing from the language menu. Listen to the recordings for the rhythm.

story.english: Yesterday I decided to learn Hindi. And today I can already speak a little Hindi.
story.roman: kal main-ne hIndee sEEkhne kaa fAIslaa kiyaa. aur AAj main abhEE se thOdee hIndee bol sAktaa hoon.
story.native: कल मैंने हिंदी सीखने का फ़ैसला किया। और आज मैं अभी से थोड़ी हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ।

feminine.roman: kal main-ne hIndee sEEkhne kaa fAIslaa kiyaa. aur AAj main abhEE se thOdee hIndee bol sAktee hoon.
feminine.native: कल मैंने हिंदी सीखने का फ़ैसला किया। और आज मैं अभी से थोड़ी हिंदी बोल सकती हूँ।

phrases.note: Kal can mean yesterday or tomorrow. The past tense in our story tells you it means yesterday.

phrases.note: Abhee se conveys ‘already, at this early stage’ in our story.
